[Package]
Name="gpower_lib_error"
Version="2014.0.0.38"
Release=""
ID=c3e0f4db08b0c8d9f83b261267fff407
File Format="vip"
Format Version="2014"
Display Name="GPower Error & Warning"


[Description]
Description="This toolset offers functions for defining dynamic global descriptions for error codes, for setting errors and warnings, for appending errors and warnings (as opposed to merging them), and to extract information from the error cluster - all in compact easy to use subVIs."
Summary="Error and warning conversion, dynamic definition and modification toolset."
License="BSD"
Copyright="Copyright (c) 2014, GPower"
Distribution=""
Vendor="GPower"
URL="www.gpower.as/error"
Packager="Steen Schmidt"
Demo="FALSE"
Release Notes="v2014 2/12 2014\0A- ToString now embeds timestamp if present as well.\0A- Bugfix: GetSource and SetTimestamp would not handle timestamps within an empty source string correctly.\0A- Big performance improvement to the IsError function.\0A- Minor icon updates.\0A- Minor VI Description clarifications.\0A\0Av2012.3 16/2 2014\0A- Added new function ToString.\0A\0Av2012.2 16/12 2013\0A- Fixed a bug where ClearError could seemingly break dataflow due to inlining.\0A\0Av2012.1 16/11 2013\0A- Now allows install on Linux and Macintosh in addition to Windows.\0A\0Av2012 8/9 2013\0A- Changed to versioning that follows the base LabVIEW version.\0A\0Av3.0 18/7 2013\0A- Added new function ErrorsEqual.\0A- Added new function FilterRecurring.\0A- Added new function FilterRepeating.\0A- Added new function GetTimestamp.\0A- Added new function SetTimestamp.\0A- ErrorType can now report three new types of errors: 'Appended errors', 'Appended warnings', and 'Appended mixed'.\0A- The default setting of the optional 'Only append if new?' input on AppendErrors has been changed from False to True.\0A- AppendErrors might now change the order of the appended errors since it'll aim to have at least one error on top of any warnings in the appended error collection. This is to eliminate the risk of getting an appended error wire value wrongfully overwritten by a built-in LabVIEW function.\0A- ClearWarning, GetExplanation, IsWarning, SetError, SetWarning, and ToWarning now supports appended errors.\0A- AppendErrors is now able to append appended errors.\0A- SetDescription is now also able to set descriptions on warnings in addition to on errors.\0A- GetSource now strips any time info from source string.\0A- Major performance optimizations (up to 200x for certain functions).\0A- Icons throughout the toolset have been updated, in some instances to make it easier to grab the VIs on the BD.\0A- IsError and IsWarning functions have new connector panes due to new icons.\0A- DefineCustomCode, GetCode, GetDescription, GetExplanation, GetSource, and UndefineCustomCode have new connector panes due to 'Error out' being removed from these functions as they do not modify the error wire.\0A- The ErrorInOut control is no longer embedded in an Error & Warning subpalette, but is available directly from the GPower controls palette.\0A\0Av2.0 19/11 2012\0A- Added new function IsWarning.\0A- GetStatus function renamed to IsError.\0A- Added support for appended errors in the FilterCodes functions.\0A- Added 'Code filtered?' output to the FilterCodes functions.\0A- Added 'Append timestamp?' input to the SetError and SetWarning functions.\0A- Added 'Label' input to the SetError, SetWarning, and SetDescription functions.\0A- Added 'Only append if new?' input to the AppendErrors functions.\0A- Added a controls palette from which you can grab both 'Error in' and 'Error out' controls at the same time.\0A- Changed recommended/required setting on some 'Error in' inputs.\0A- Changed several VIs to run as subroutine to allow some of these functions to be used in subroutine callers.\0A- Moved this toolset into an lvlib. This breaks function paths backwards compatibility.\0A- 'Label' input on the DefineCustomCode funtion changed position on the connector pane.\0A- Minor updates to some icons.\0A- Fixed a minor bug were the default label was not set on custom errors.\0A- Fixed a minor bug were a label could be set with an empty description string on custom errors.\0A- Toolset renamed from 'Error' to 'Error & Warning'.\0A\0Av1.2 9/1 2012\0A- Changed namespace of toolset from 'Error - ' to 'Error_' to eliminate spaces in VI names.\0A- ConvertToWarning function renamed to ToWarning.\0A- Added global dynamic error definitions with the new DefineCustomCode and UndefineCustomCode functions.\0A- Added appending errors and warnings (as opposed to merging) with the new AppendErrors and SplitAppended functions.\0A- Added GetDescription and SetDescription functions.\0A- Updated the SetError and SetWarning functions to always set call chain as source.\0A- Deleted the GetCodeAndSource function as this was basically just one of many combinations where none of the others are implemented.\0A- Replaced the Source input with a Description input on the SetError and SetWarning functions.\0A- In general changed this toolset's understanding of the source string of an error cluster from a generic string to the proper Source and Description fields within that string. This is to support appending to and replacing built-in error descriptions. The documentation is updated to explain this in detail.\0A\0Av1.1 15/10 2011\0A- Added new function GetStatus.\0A- Added descriptions to all controls and indicators.\0A- Added access to user guide from detailed help in all VIs.\0A\0Av1.0 4/8 2011\0A- Initial public release."

[Package] Name="ls_instruments_ag_lib_lv_websockets" Version="1.8.0.5" Release="" ID=827c098ed2c456ff7e35ceed86858c59 File Format="vip" Format Version="2017" Display Name="LV-WebSockets" [Description] Description="This library is a fork of v1.6.0.22 of the WebSokets library by MediaMongrels Ltd.\0A\0AThe main new feature is the introduction of support for resource names as per RFC 6455 and better adherence to the RFC standard.\0A\0AAs far as the author knows, this is the only LabVIEW WebSocket library supporting resource names. \0A\0AThe library leverages on the TCP VIs for establishing a WebSocket connection and communicating through it. It allows, for example, a web browser to communicate with a LabVIEW application acting as a WebSocket server.\0A\0AIt contains VIs for performing WebSocket handshaking, reading/writing data and closing the connection. The API allows for you to write code to act as both a WebSocket server, and as a client.\0A\0ASince the fork the following changes have been implemented:\0A\0A* Fixed bugs in client handshake code:\0A* Refactored the client/server handshake code\0A* added support for WebSocket resources names as per RFC 6455\0A* Now the server handshake checks if a resource is available as of the input array of resource and it answers with a 404 Not Found HTTP response according to the RFC 6455. Server handshake similarly handles the malformed client handshake by answering with a 400 Bad Request HTTP response according to RFC 6455. We added a "ProcessHandshakeResponse.vi" that fully checks the server response as of RFC 6455, before there was only a partial check obtained by reusing "the ProcessHandshakeRequest.vi"server code.\0A* Data Framing Refactoring: Introduced a generic "SendDataFrame.vi" which sends a data frame according to all the possible Opcodes as defined "Opcodes.ctl" enum and also allows to set the Final Frame Bit (FIN Bit). This vi is now used in both the "Write.vi" and "Close.vi", as well as the newly introduced "Ping.vi" and "Pong.vi". \0A* The "Close.vi" now correctly sets the FIN bit and allows to send a Close Status as defined in the "StatusCode.ctl" ring and a close reason\0A* A "DecodeCloseReason.vi" was introduced to decode the Close Status and the reason as delivered by the "Read.vi"\0A* The "Write.vi" now can send binary an text data frames. \0A* The "Read.vi" was refactored so as to allow also binary data, to read the FIN bit and the close reason in case of receive "Connection Close" opcode. As a result now the calling code has the tools to handle the multi-framing and the Ping/Pong exchanges.\0A* Introduced an enum typedef defining the data format type either text or binary.\0A* added a VI to create a valid WebSocket URI staring from IP address, port and service name. \0A* The close method now filters error 6066 originating from the waiting Read method when the peer closes the connection. This allows now for a clean connection close" Summary="A library implementing the WebSocket protocol including support for resource names" License="MIT" Copyright="Copyright (c) 2023, LS Instruments AG" Distribution="" Vendor="LS Instruments AG" URL="https://github.com/LS-Instruments/LV-WebSockets" Packager="Andrea Vaccaro" Demo="FALSE" Release Notes="- Improved error handling in client handshake\0A- Implemented URI parsing for wss/https URIs\0A- Implemented support for Secure WebSocket\0A- Now if the client/server handshaking fails the TCP connection will be closed\0A- Up to now, the Sec-WebSocket-Key was a value hard-coded in the code. Implemented the generation of a random 16 bytes string and then its encoding to a 24 bytes Base64 string as specified in the RFC 6455 . This will improve the security of the implementation\0A- Minor improvement to the example code\0A- The previous implementation of the Base64 encoding was relatively slow and inefficient. We have replaced it with a highly optimized pure LabVIEW implementations available here https://forums.ni.com/t5/Example-Code/Fast-Base64-Encoder-Decoder-using-LabVIEW/ta-p/3503281.\0A- As per RFC 2616 (referred in RFC 6455) headers should be matched in a case insensitive manner. This is was not done and caused a problem with certain WebSocket servers. We have implemented a case insensitive header matching."
